title: A running chat says what its turn waits on — another conversation's write, the previous request's changes being saved, the page being looked at — instead of only "Thinking for…"
steps: S1: waitOutLease against a lease refused twice then free, refused until the bound, a free site, and a send that throws.
S2: The shared wait record: begin, read, end; a newer wait over an older one; whileWaiting over a promise that resolves and one that rejects; a second copy of the module.
S3: The shipped site-tabs plugin: a first write waiting for the turn's open.
S4: The shipped site-tools plugin's /held door asked with wait: true while a lease wait is recorded for the conversation, and without it.
S5: The chat line mounted: a running chat whose host says lease 12 s, the turn ending, an idle chat, a running one with no wait or a 1 s one.
expect: S1: marked once and unmarked once whenever it waited, even when a send throws; never marked for a free site.
S2: whole seconds while it lasts, null after; the newer wait stays when the older ends; one record whichever copy asks.
S3: the conversation reads 'previous' while the write waits, null once it went.
S4: waiting {kind: lease, seconds: 7} for wait: true, null with nothing recorded; the plain answer has no waiting key.

S5: [data-chat-wait=lease] "Waiting for another conversation to finish changing this site… 12 s" (never a name), gone when the turn ends with no more asks; nothing asked while idle; nothing drawn for no wait or a short one.
evidence: Plan #1403 item 10 (code read 16/10/2026): a write waits up to 100 s for another conversation's lease (lease-wait.mjs), the first write up to 120 s for the turn's open (writeReady), a turn that wrote up to 30 s for the visual check — the model works in none of them and the chat showed only "Thinking for…"
fence: The door says what is waited on and for how long, never who; asked only by a running chat, with wait: true

tests: the wait is marked once when the first refusal makes it wait, and unmarked when it ends, however it ends
a wait is read with its whole seconds, and gone once ended; ending twice is nothing
a newer wait of the conversation is the one shown; ending the older leaves it
whileWaiting marks the wait for as long as the promise runs, a rejection included; no session marks nothing
one record per process, whichever copy of the module asks (each plugin bundles its own)
a write waiting for the previous request to be saved is marked as that wait, and unmarked when it goes
the shipped plugin leases a running turn, holds a follow-up while draining, and tells its author
waitLine: a known wait long enough to look stuck gets its line; anything else none
readWait asks the held door with wait: true; a refusal, a foreign body or no answer is nothing
a running chat whose turn waits on another conversation says so, with the seconds; never who
an idle chat asks nothing; a running one with no wait, or a short one, draws nothing
